text:
Priya: Quick check — we're seeing lots of clients doing immediate retries on 429/5xx and spamming the serving layer. Need a short, language-agnostic guidance we can copy into SDK READMEs: recommended backoff window, when to consider a request non-retryable (idempotency rules), and streaming-specific resume advice. cc @Kevin @Liu

Kevin: TL;DR guidance we usually give:
- 429: respect Retry-After when present, otherwise exponential backoff with jitter.
- 5xx: backoff too but prefer faster failover for persistent 5xx (circuit breaker).
- Non-idempotent operations (POSTs with side effects): require explicit Idempotency-Key to safely retry.

Liu: More concrete numbers that have worked in prod for PLG + enterprise mix:
- initial delay 200ms +/- 50% jitter, multiplier x2, cap at 10s, max attempts 6 (including the original).
- On repeated 429 spikes, increase cap to 30s after 3 consecutive 429s to avoid thrash.
- For 5xx, consider max attempts 4 and trigger client-side circuit open for 30s after >5 failures in 1m.

Sam: For streaming (chunked responses / server-sent events / long HTTP streams) — what to do when a connection drops mid-stream?

Liu: Streaming rules:
- Provide resume tokens from server at chunk boundaries. Clients must include last-seen seq in reconnect headers.
- If no resume token, treat stream reconnect as a fresh session (do NOT replay client-side actions that caused side effects unless idempotency is guaranteed).
- For languages without strong streaming libs, document a simple reconnect flow:
```
# reconnect pseudo
POST /v1/stream?resume_token=abc123
Headers: Resume-Token: abc123
```

Priya: Auth race question — some SDKs retry immediately after a 401 while another thread is already refreshing the token, causing duplicate refreshes / token races. Recommended pattern?

Kevin: Single-flight token refresh: first retrying caller triggers refresh and other callers wait (or use the new token when available). If waiting isn't possible, allow one retry per caller but limit to 1 immediate retry post-refresh. Avoid blind infinite retries on 401.

Sam: Language-specific quirks — Node: timers/jitter skew under load; Go: goroutine storms recreating many connections. Any wording to add to SDK READMEs?

Liu: Add short notes per SDK:
- Node: use setTimeout-based jitter and avoid 0ms sleeps; consider progressive backoff with setImmediate fallback.
- Go: use a bounded worker pool for retries to avoid goroutine storms; prefer context cancellation on long waits.

Priya: Example header for idempotency so product folks can copy:
```
POST /v1/infer
Headers:
  Idempotency-Key: 6f1b2a9e-...
  Content-Type: application/json
Body: { prompt: "..." }
```
If Idempotency-Key missing, SDK should mark POST as non-retryable by default.

Kevin: Also call out the difference between Retry-After (server-suggested) and client-side cap. Respect Retry-After strictly, but still apply client-side max attempts to avoid infinite slow retries.

DevExBot: Short doc link: https://go.redwood.ai/devex/retries-guidance (internal) — includes example code for Node/Go/Python + a sample state machine for stream resume. :link:

Priya: Thanks — I'm going to draft a 2-paragraph section for each SDK and ping for reviews. If we can standardize the numbers above (200ms start, x2, cap 10s, max 6) that's 👍 :thumbsup:

Liu: Works for me. I'll add the single-flight token snippet for Go and Node tomorrow.

Sam: I'll update the streaming example in the JS SDK to include Resume-Token header handling.

Kevin: Cool — once merged we should announce in #devex and add a small blurb to the Public SDK README (non-sensitive parts).
